title: Service integrity audit summary and customer replay offer
body:
TL;DR: This draft is a customer-facing summary and opt-in replay offer following the 2029-01-11 cross-region inference integrity incident. It is intended for the status page update + a follow-up customer email.

Purpose: provide a short plain-language timeline, the root-cause synopsis, what we fixed, how customers can verify their data and optionally request a replay of affected requests, and the compensation/next-steps options. Keep it concise but transparent.

Suggested status-page short blurb (<= 300 chars):
  - 2029-01-11 02:40 UTC — Resolved: We investigated a degradation that caused intermittent stale or duplicated responses for a subset of requests. Root cause: cache coordination bug during autoscaler fallback. No evidence of data loss. Customers can request a replay of affected inference windows. More details & opt-in link in full post.

Customer-facing postmortem (expanded)
1) Incident summary (plain language)
  - What happened: Between 2029-01-11 01:17 UTC and 2029-01-11 02:40 UTC, some inference requests returned stale or duplicated tokens/outputs. This affected a small fraction of requests in multi-tenant pools during a capacity-rebalancing event.
  - Scope: ~0.7% of requests in affected pools; 42 tenants had at least one request in the affected window; no customer data exfiltration observed.

2) Root cause (concise)
  - Sequence: During an autoscaler-triggered node drain (capacity rebalance), replicas serving cached KV prefixes were evicted and reattached. A race in the cache replica coordination code allowed a mismatched KV prefix to be used for a short period. The result: a small number of requests read stale KV states leading to repeated or truncated continuations.
  - Contributing factors: (a) fallback path in Dedicated routing didn't fully invalidate per-replica caches, (b) a recently deployed optimization for fast rejoin (PR #4321) had a regression in replica epoch handling, (c) our alert thresholds did not surface the specific token-repeat signal fast enough.

3) Impact to customers
  - Correctness: Some completions contained duplicated phrases or premature truncation; in a few cases partial hallucinations were amplified by repeated prefix state.
  - Availability: No broad availability loss — API endpoints remained reachable. Some requests required client-side retries.
  - Data integrity: No evidence of data corruption at rest; logs and traces are intact.

4) Mitigation and fixes deployed (what we changed immediately)
  - Emergency rollback of PR #4321 at 2029-01-11 02:01 UTC.
  - Forced cache invalidation across the affected Dedicated pools at 2029-01-11 02:10 UTC.
  - Added a short-term safeguard in the routing layer to keep clients on stable replicas while rejoin completes (hotfix v0.9.14).
  - Added a token-repeat detector to our alerting (rule: > 0.5% token duplication rate => Pager).
  - Long-term: patch landed to remove the epoch race and an integration test that simulates concurrent evict/rejoin sequences. ETA for rollout: 2029-01-25.

5) How customers can verify and optionally request a replay
  - Verification checklist (self-serve):
    * Check logs for duplicate-token markers (we flag these as event tag: "kv-repeat" in traces).
    * If you saw truncated or obviously duplicated responses, note timestamps (UTC) and request IDs if available.
  - Opt-in replay offer (what we provide):
    * We can re-run affected inference requests on pinned model versions using preserved inputs from the time window 2029-01-11 01:15:00 — 2029-01-11 02:45:00 UTC.
    * Replays are free and run with a strict data handling policy: replays are isolated, do not affect production rate limits, and are logged in a separate evidence pack.
    * To request a replay, customers must:
      1. Fill the replay request form (link placeholder: <replay-form-url>) with tenant ID, desired window (defaults above), and consent checkbox confirming re-execution of inputs.
      2. Optionally indicate if you prefer side-by-side comparison or replacement of original results.
    * Turnaround: typical turnaround 48–72 business hours after verification.

6) Evidence & verification package we provide
  - For each replay request we will provide: request IDs, original traces, sanitized inputs, re-execution logs, and a concise diff report highlighting differences between original and replayed outputs.
  - We will redact any customer PII per your Data Processing Agreement; replays happen in a temporary isolated tenant.

7) Compensation & remediation options
  - For confirmed integrity-impact cases: a one-time credit equivalent to two days of average inference charges for affected tenants (automatic for tenants with verified differences).
  - If replay demonstrates material correctness regression that impacted product functionality, CS will escalate for case-by-case contractual remediation.

8) Communications plan / suggested emails
  - Short status page entry (see top).
  - Follow-up email template for affected tenants (short):
    Subject: "Redwood Inference — Replay offer & integrity summary for Jan 11 incident"
    Body: "We investigated and resolved a short issue that may have affected some inference outputs on Jan 11. We offer a free replay of affected requests and a verification package. Click <replay-form-url> to request a replay. Your CS rep (cc'd) can help. — Sasha, Customer Success"

9) Open actions / internal notes
  - Verify that evidence export tooling supports bulk tenant packages (owner: infra-data, due: 2029-01-20).
  - SRE: finalize and run chaos test that simulates node rejoin + cache eviction (owner: eng-sre, due: 2029-01-22).
  - Product: evaluate whether routing can surface degraded-token signals into a tenant-facing metric (owner: product-hosted-api, due: 2029-02-05).

10) Risk & FAQs (for CS reps)
  - Q: Will replays expose customer inputs to humans?
    A: No. Replays run in an automated, isolated environment with the same KMS/tenant isolation we use in production. Only the minimal CS/investigation team sees sanitized evidence if needed.
  - Q: Could replay produce different results?
    A: Yes — replays may differ because they are run against corrected cache/cohort state. If differences materially change outcomes you rely on, we will escalate.

11) Suggested next-status updates cadence
  - Immediate (status page): short blurb + link to this post (published now).
  - Follow-up (48 hours): update with number of replay requests received and any systemic findings.
  - Closure (post replay window complete): summary of replays completed, number with material diffs, and confirmation of final fixes rolled out.

Draft checklist before publish:
  - Legal review of replay consent language (owner: legal, check: DPA compatibility).
  - Final security review confirming isolation procedures.
  - CS review of compensation rubric.

Notes to self (rough):
  - We should include a short public graph showing the duplication rate spike (redacted axes) — ask Observability to produce a tenant-agnostic image.
  - Consider pre-populating replay form with tenant usage window suggestions when we detect request IDs in customer logs.

Contact: Sasha Lin (sasha@redwood.ai) — Customer Success lead for this incident.

---
Internal backlinks / bookmarks: CONFLUENCE-1254 (audit notes), JIRA-8482 (bug), GH PR #4321 (rollback candidate).

End of draft.

Unresolved questions to discuss in review:
  - Should the replay window be extended to +/- 30 minutes for tenants with sparse logs? pros/cons.
  - Threshold for "material correctness" that triggers extra remediation (legal input required).
  - Decide whether to auto-offer credits vs. require verification that a customer experienced visible degradation.

(Keep this doc as the canonical customer-facing draft; final wording will be copied into status page entry and tenant email template once legal signs off.)
